Updated

The only reason that I recommend this change is because this is the behavior that I am used to from other Postgres connection poolers.

For example with pgcat:
```console
user@host:~$ pgcat --version
pgcat 1.1.2-dev4
user@host:~$ psql  'postgresql://pgcat:pgcat@localhost:6433/pgbouncer'
psql (15.7, server 1.1.2-dev4)
WARNING: psql major version 15, server major version 1.1.
         Some psql features might not work.
```

Or with PgBouncer:
```console
user@host:~$ pgbouncer --version
PgBouncer 1.23.1
libevent 2.1.12-stable
adns: c-ares 1.15.0
tls: OpenSSL 3.0.1 14 Dec 2021
systemd: yes
user@host:~$ psql  'postgresql://postgres@localhost:6432/pgbouncer'
psql (15.7, server 1.23.1/bouncer)
WARNING: psql major version 15, server major version 1.23.
         Some psql features might not work.
```

It is nice to see the actual version number of the service that you are connecting to instead of an arbitrary 9.6.0. It is also nice to see an additional sanity check that you are not actually connected to a postgres database server but a connection pooler admin console.

This is just my 2 cents, feel free to close this PR if you do not agree with my rationale.
